chunks.content: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 on 2025-05-08 — the "Claude 4" family: Opus 4 the flagship ("Claude 4"), Sonnet 4 the fast workhorse. Pricing: Opus 4 at $15 / $75 per million tokens (input/output), Sonnet 4 at $3 / $15 — Sonnet priced as the developer-default coding model. The headline capability was agentic coding and computer use: Claude 4's "computer use 2.0" (browser control) was roughly twice as reliable as the 3.x generation's, and the launch was timed to the rise of Claude Code as the defining agentic-coding product of 2025. The 4.1 update (2025-06-18) improved coding and agentic reliability at the same prices; the naming ("4.1" rather than "4.5") followed a reported internal dispute about Anthropic's version-naming policy. The direct competitive context was the OpenAI o-series and the enterprise agentic-coding gold rush; Anthropic positioned Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent and reported record API usage. Driven by Claude Code adoption, Anthropic raised a large funding round in late September 2025 at a reported ~$183 billion valuation, cementing its position as the coding-agent leader.

prior_gap_texts: Anthropic released the Claude 4 family on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

The launch included two distinct models to serve different market segments and use cases:

*   **Claude Opus 4:** Positioned as the flagship model ("Claude 4"), it was priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

*   **Claude Sonnet 4:** Positioned as a "fast workhorse" and the developer-default coding model, it was significantly cheaper at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

The decision to release these specific tiers signaled that Anthropic viewed agentic coding as its primary competitive battleground against OpenAI’s o-series in an enterprise "agentic-coding gold rush" [Source: ev-1].

By highlighting capabilities such as "computer use 2.0," which was roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation's browser control, Anthropic positioned Claude 4 as the safest and most reliable coding agent available [Source: ev-1].

This strategy aimed to capture both high-end performance needs with Opus and volume-driven developer adoption with Sonnet, a move that contributed to record API usage and helped cement Anthropic’s position as a leader in the coding-agent market [Source: ev-1].
